analyst_view.overall: Benfica top the Europa League with four wins from four and want to secure a top-eight place; Viktoria Plzen are 30th with 3 points but have won four of their last five games, and Radoslav Kovac says almost his whole squad is fit. Benfica's 24-man squad (Record, A Bola) leaves out Prestianni (lower back pain) and Aursnes (thigh, close to a return), neither of which the numbers know, plus Barreiro, who is already counted; young right-back Banjaqui travels. Marco Silva still has Pavlidis, Lukebakio, Rafa Silva, Sudakov, Schjelderup and Jhon Duran, and Plzen miss only Jemelka (counted). Croatian referee Igor Pajac has a very low card rate, which the numbers already take off, and a frosty night is expected in Plzen on a pitch said to be in excellent shape. No new news this morning, so I keep the small trim on Benfica's attack for Prestianni.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, 1.9 for Benfica, already nudged up for their scoring run and down for Barreiro. Prestianni, who scored on Sunday, stayed in Lisbon with back pain and the numbers don't know it; Benfica still have Pavlidis, Lukebakio and Rafa Silva, so I trim only slightly, to about 2.6.

corners.text: The numbers expect 8.9 corners, with Benfica pushing (5.1) and a small trim for Plzen conceding few corners lately. Benfica's wide play with Lukebakio and Schjelderup is the usual pattern the numbers know, and losing Prestianni and Aursnes changes the names more than the approach, so I stay at about 8.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards: Benfica's high recent card count adds (+12.7%), but referee Igor Pajac, at 2.7 cards a game, takes about 17% off. Plzen will have to stop Benfica's runners in front of a full home crowd, which the numbers already assume, so I stay at about 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers expect 28.1 shots, already adding for Plzen's busy recent attack (+8.3%). Benfica lose Prestianni, one of their most active shooters, and Aursnes, while Plzen are near full strength, so I trim slightly to about 27.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target, already adding for both sides' accurate recent shooting. Without Prestianni, Benfica's attack leans more on Pavlidis and Lukebakio, so I trim a little, to about 10.3.
